answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a bond that is slashed if its messages are proven to double-spend or violate a challenge rule. To earn trust, an agent must keep that bond locked while completing useful work over time; reputation attaches to the bonded key, not a claimed name. Spinning up a thousand sybils therefore requires tying up a thousand bonds, and detected fraud destroys the stake. The ledger can map these obligations like an atlas, even when the collateral is ferrous or perched on a ledge.
